items.questionText:
A moral dilemma involves making a choice between two or more moral values whereby in making a decision, or in taking action, you will compromise or violate some other moral {1}. A moral dilemma is a situation that involves a choice, decision or action to solve an unpleasant problem that we need to {2}.

A response to a moral dilemma is not always a matter of "right {3} wrong", as both courses of action could seem moral (or the "right thing to do"). This involves having to decide the best way to respond when faced with two or more "right" courses of action. When faced with a moral dilemma, you will probably be asking yourself "What should I do?". You may have a "little voice" inside your head telling you to do one thing, while your immediate desire is to do another. Some may refer to this "little voice" as your conscience, and it is impossible to {4} it. Consequently, these dilemmas are often very difficult to resolve.

As an example, imagine that your eighteen-year-old son/daughter {5} to you that they had been involved in the recent theft of your neighbor’s car. Should you call the police? Maybe you should turn your son/daughter in because you want to be honest with you neighbor and you feel that your child must not be allowed to escape {6}. Or should you simply "keep quiet" because you want to remain {7} to your son/daughter, especially since your child told everything to you in confidence?

Moral dilemmas are part of our every day life and we should always keep in mind that our moral compass is our conscience.
